speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I see you're here for wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; can you describe how the skin lesions look and where they are located on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota, have you noticed any expanding red rash with a central clearing, often described as a "bull's-eye," on your skin?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those painless violaceous lesions on your hands and wrists are a very specific and concerning sign, distinct from the typical bull's-eye rash. Have you experienced any shortness of breath, cough, or confusion, and do you recall seeing any ticks during your camping trip?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of migratory arthritis, violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands, and fever is highly suggestive of disseminated gonococcal infection. I will now request a Gram stain and culture of the joint fluid to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Joint Fluid Gram Stain and Culture
